original_title: The role of population-based model selection using non-linear mixed-effects modeling in a preclinical study of [(177)Lu]Lu-EDTMP.
title: Picking the right PK model for Lu-177-EDTMP
blurb: A preclinical study using population-based nonlinear mixed-effects modeling to choose among competing pharmacokinetic models for Lu-177-EDTMP, the bone-seeking radiopharmaceutical. Model-selection housekeeping, but the kind that decides whether the dosimetry numbers downstream can be trusted.

original_title: Targeted Radiopharmaceuticals for Synovitis: Emerging Molecular Imaging and Theranostic Perspectives.
title: Imaging and treating synovitis with the oncology radiopharma playbook
blurb: A review applying targeted molecular imaging and theranostic strategies, borrowed from oncology, to synovitis specifically. A perspective piece laying out the ambition rather than new data.

original_title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines
title: One diene, one amine, either stereochemistry you want
blurb: Stereodivergent telomerization steers the same linear functionalized diene and amine pairing to either stereochemical outcome on demand, instead of locking you into whatever the catalyst happens to default to. Switchable stereocontrol on a telomerization isn't something that's normally available to order.

original_title: Implementation and Real-World Outcomes of [(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 for Metastatic Androgen Pathway Modulation-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Following Public Reimbursement in Canada.
title: Lu-177-PSMA-617 outside the trial bubble, this time in Canada
blurb: Real-world outcomes for Lu-177-PSMA-617 in androgen-pathway-resistant metastatic prostate cancer, gathered after Canada's public payers started covering it. Post-reimbursement data is the useful kind, actual patients instead of trial-selected ones.

original_title: A General Approach to Cyclogeranyl Terpenoids: Total Synthesis of (±)- and (+)-Maximumin C and Synthesis of Saldigitin A Core
title: One stereochemical trick, two terpenoid cores
blurb: An Eschenmoser-Claisen rearrangement followed by amide-directed hydrogenation sets the awkward trans 5α-H/10β-Me stereochemistry on the A ring, and that one sequence is general enough to deliver both the full synthesis of maximumin C and the gnarlier [6–7–6] tricyclic core behind saldigitin A's benzocycloheptane. Solve the stereochemistry once, reuse it across the whole terpenoid family.

original_title: DNA-Encoded Libraries: Advances in Library Encoding, Construction, and Applications in Targeted Theranostics
title: DNA-encoded libraries grow up, now aimed at theranostics
blurb: A perspective tracking DEL technology past plain hit-finding: better DNA-compatible chemistry, more library architectures (linear, branched, cyclic, late-stage natural-product), and ligands now being pulled out for radionuclide drug conjugates, chemical inducers of proximity, and bispecific cell engagers. A roundup, not new data, but a useful map of where DEL hits actually end up.

original_title: Transition‐Metal‐Catalyzed Chelation‐Assisted C(sp 2)─H Activation/Annulation for the Synthesis of Seven‐Membered N/O‐Heterocycles
title: Building seven-membered rings off a directing group, three ways
blurb: A review of C–H activation routes to seven-membered N/O-heterocycles, sorted by how the ring closes: [5+2], [4+3], or [6+1] combinations of catalyst, directing group, and coupling partner. A map of what's been done that's also honest about where the current strategies still come up short.

original_title: Interchangeability of PSMA PET Tracers and Theranostic Target Efficacy in Prostate Cancer.
title: Are all PSMA PET tracers really interchangeable?
blurb: A review asking whether swapping one PSMA PET tracer for another still predicts theranostic target efficacy the same way in prostate cancer. Matters once that scan is deciding who gets Lu-177-PSMA-617, not just producing a pretty image.

original_title: Asymmetric Synthesis of [2,3]‐Fused Indole Heterocycles via Rh(II)/Chiral Phosphoric Acid‐Catalyzed Intramolecular C–H Insertions
title: A chiral proton shuttle steers carbene C-H insertion into indoles
blurb: Rh(II) carbene insertion into the C-H bonds of indolyl diazo compounds, with a chiral phosphoric acid doing double duty as a proton-transfer shuttle to set the stereochemistry. The result is a broad set of enantioenriched fused indole heterocycles in good yield and high ee, including some late-stage substrates.

original_title: An Ortho-Fluorinated Nucleobase Surrogate for G-Quadruplex-Based Fluorescence Sensing and 19F NMR Detection of Hydrogen Peroxide
title: A GFP-mimic nucleotide that lights up when it meets hydrogen peroxide
blurb: A fluorinated nucleobase surrogate sits dark inside a G-quadruplex DNA loop until H2O2 strips off its boronate mask, releasing a fluorescent phenolate and about a 17-fold signal jump at low-micromolar peroxide. The fluorine also gives you a 19F NMR readout, so it's a sensor with two channels built in.

original_title: Characterizing Material Mechanics and Modeling Variability in Organic Hydrogels: A Framework for Soft and Biodegradable Robotics
title: Hydrogels are inconsistent, so here's a framework for measuring exactly how
blurb: Biologically-derived hydrogels used in soft robotics and biofabrication swing wildly in mechanical behavior depending on polymer batch and print conditions. Rather than report another hydrogel, this builds a framework for characterizing and modeling that variability itself, the unglamorous work actually needed before any of these parts are reproducible.

original_title: Efficacy of radionuclide therapy in the treatment of inoperable or metastatic pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
title: Does radionuclide therapy actually help in inoperable pheo and para
blurb: An efficacy look at radionuclide therapy for inoperable or metastatic pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, tumors with a thin options list once surgery isn't on the table.

original_title: Test-retest repeatability of deep learning-enabled quantitative PET parameters and PROMISE criteria-based lesion index in 18F-DCFPyL PSMA-PET/CT
title: Checking if AI-scored PSMA-PET numbers hold still on a second scan
blurb: Test-retest repeatability of deep learning-derived quantitative PET parameters and a PROMISE-criteria lesion index on 18F-DCFPyL PSMA-PET/CT. Unglamorous but necessary: before anyone trusts these numbers for monitoring disease, they need to not jump around between scans of the same patient.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen-Targeted Phototherapy for Prostate Cancer: A Systematic Review of Preclinical Evidence and Translational Readiness.
title: PSMA-targeted phototherapy for prostate cancer, graded on how close it actually is
blurb: A systematic review of the preclinical evidence behind PSMA-targeted phototherapy for prostate cancer, framed around translational readiness rather than just cataloguing light-activated constructs. The useful part is the readiness verdict, not another list of candidates.

original_title: 18F-Labeled 7-Azaindole-Based Radioligands for Imaging Colony-Stimulating Factor 1 Receptor in Glioblastoma.
title: New 18F tracers aimed at CSF1R, not the glioblastoma cells themselves
blurb: 18F-labeled 7-azaindole radioligands built to image colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor, a marker on the tumor-associated macrophages that pack glioblastoma, rather than the tumor cells. Imaging the immune infiltrate instead of the tumor is the interesting bit here.

original_title: Overriding Polarity Mismatch in Radical Difunctionalization of 1,3‐Dienes
title: Making radicals add where polarity says they shouldn't
blurb: Radical additions to electron-deficient 1,3-dienes are supposed to obey polarity matching and hit C4. This three-component 1,4-dicarbofunctionalization pairs them with alpha-aminoalkyl radicals to force the mismatched, previously unexplored C1-selective addition instead.

original_title: Molar-mass- and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules via iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of α-substituted acrylates
title: Vinyl polymers built one exact unit at a time
blurb: An iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of alpha-substituted acrylates that grows vinyl macromolecules with both molar mass and monomer sequence precisely defined, treating a vinyl chain less like a radical free-for-all and more like a stepwise synthesis.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Desymmetrizing Endo-Cyclization for the Construction of P-Stereogenic Centers
title: Palladium picks one of two identical vinyl arms to build P-stereogenic centers
blurb: A chiral phosphoramidite-ligated Pd catalyst desymmetrizes prochiral 2-bromoaryldivinylphosphine oxides, telling apart two enantiotopic vinyl groups and pushing the harder endo-cyclization path to build P-stereogenic benzophosphole oxides in good yield and high enantiomeric ratio, no external coupling partner required.

original_title: Construction of Amide-Containing Dihydropyrroles through Palladium-Catalyzed Aza-Heck Carbonylation
title: Skipping the CO tank for amide dihydropyrroles
blurb: A Pd-catalyzed aza-Heck carbonylation that swaps gaseous CO for solid Mo(CO)6 as the carbonyl source, giving amide-containing dihydropyrroles in moderate to good yields. Mostly a safety and handling win, you get precise stoichiometric CO control instead of a gas line, plus a decent substrate scope and products that can be elaborated further.

original_title: Control of axial stereochemistry for the enantioselective construction of a QUINAP library
title: Finally a clean way to build out a QUINAP library
blurb: QUINAP's been a workhorse chiral P,N-ligand for years, but making a real library of variants with high ee was underdeveloped. This gets there in two steps from racemic QUINOLs, using solvent-dependent crystallization-induced deracemization under heat to lock in the axial stereochemistry. A crystallization trick doing the enantioselective heavy lifting.

original_title: Telix (ASX:TLX): Why This ASX 200 Biotech Is Chasing Isotope Supply - Kalkine Media
title: Telix is chasing isotope supply, not a new result
blurb: A market write-up on why the ASX-listed radiopharma company is scrambling to lock down isotope supply deals. Investor framing rather than science, but isotope supply is the genuine bottleneck underneath most of this field's hype.

original_title: Synthetic Control of Quantum Phases in Organic Conductors: Molecular-Level Disorder Engineering and Pressure-Induced Superconductivity
title: Isolating what disorder alone does to a superconductor
blurb: Molecular conductors are flexible enough that you can grow crystals with controlled structural randomness without doping or touching the band structure, so this platform gets a clean split between an ordered superconducting phase and a disordered insulating one from thermodynamic control during crystal growth alone. Useful precisely because doping usually muddies this comparison.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Cross-Linking the Blue: Trends in Marine-Based Hydrogels.
title: A survey of marine-derived hydrogels
blurb: A review piece on cross-linking trends in hydrogels made from marine materials. No new data here, just a lay of the land.

original_title: Hole Mobility Synchronizes Carbon Oxidation and Nitrate Reduction to Switch Photocatalytic Selectivity between Ammonia and Urea
title: Hole mobility is the dial that picks ammonia or urea
blurb: Cadmium vacancies in single-atom Cu-on-CdS cut the effective hole mass and speed up hole transport, and that alone is enough to sync carbon oxidation with nitrate reduction and flip the product from ammonia to urea. The carbon side comes from oxidative cleavage of biomass-derived oxalic acid, so it's turning waste carbon and nitrate runoff into something more useful than fertilizer.

original_title: Regioswitchable and Enantioselective Dialkylation of Alkenes: Modular Access to Chiral β- and γ-Amino Esters
title: Two alkyl groups, two regiochemistries, one alkene
blurb: A catalytic alkene dialkylation that installs two distinct alkyl-alkyl bonds across the C=C and can be switched between regiochemistries while staying enantioselective either way, giving chiral β- or γ-amino esters off the same modular setup. Prior methods needed directing groups or specific radical traps to get anywhere near this.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: GSDME-dependent pyroptosis potentiates c-Met-targeted ADC and PD-(L)1 blockade synergy in solid tumors.
title: Pyroptosis is the quiet booster behind a c-Met ADC/checkpoint combo
blurb: GSDME-dependent pyroptosis turns out to be what's driving the synergy between a c-Met-targeted ADC and PD-(L)1 blockade in solid tumors. A mechanistic explanation for why that combo outperforms either drug alone, worth filing away next time a checkpoint plus ADC trial reads better than expected.

original_title: Direct-inject liquid-chromatography enables an autonomous continuous preferential crystallization platform
title: Running chiral crystallization on autopilot
blurb: Continuous preferential crystallization can split a racemic mixture into both enantiomers without chiral auxiliaries, but it's been bottlenecked on real-time tracking of the enantiomeric ratio. Pairing it with direct-inject LC closes that loop and makes the whole thing run autonomously, which is the part that's actually been missing.

original_title: Taming the carbamoyl radical for selective hydrocarbamidation of alkynes via metallaphotoredox catalysis
title: Getting carbamoyl radicals to cooperate on alkynes
blurb: Ir-photoredox/Ni catalysis adds an amide group across an alkyne using carbamoyl chlorides instead of the usual formamide or isocyanate surrogates. Prior Ni-catalyzed hydrocarbamoylation and hydroamidation routes were stuck with those surrogates, which capped the range of amide partners you could use, so this should open the door a lot wider.

original_title: Engaging native carboxylic acids via solvent-gated proton relay for photo(electro)chemical decarboxylative functionalizations
title: Decarboxylation photochemistry gets a solvent-gated proton shuttle
blurb: Dibenzo-fused ketone photocatalysts pull CO2 straight off native carboxylic acids and route the resulting radicals onto N-heteroarenes under photoelectrochemical conditions, no pre-activation needed. The spectroscopy is the real find: an excited-state proton relay that only switches on in the right solvent.

original_title: Magnetic proximity effect in nanoparticle–molecule hybrids enables room-temperature circularly polarized luminescence
title: Circularly polarized light from emitters that have no chirality of their own
blurb: Room-temperature CPL usually means engineering chirality into the molecule itself. Here nanoparticle-molecule hybrids get it from magnetic proximity instead, spin transferred across the interface, and the output is field-tunable rather than fixed. Nice route into chiroptics and spintronics if the interfacial transfer proves general.

original_title: A Plug-and-Play Photoenzymatic Platform for the Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral γ -Aryl Esters
title: An empty enzyme pocket repurposed as a photocatalyst host
blurb: Flavin ene-reductases routinely lose their cofactor when expressed heterologously, so instead of fighting that they just dose the apoenzyme with exogenous FMN and use the protein shell as a preorganized host, driving asymmetric synthesis of chiral gamma-aryl esters. Binding data (a large negative heat capacity change) say the flavin is actually docked in the pocket, not just floating around acting as a free photosensitizer.

original_title: Near Autonomous Discovery of One-pot Carbon-Carbon Bond Formation through Reductive Amination and DPPH-mediated Nitrogen Deletion
title: An AI drafted the one-pot nitrogen-deletion protocol, chemists just checked the work
blurb: Reductive amination followed by DPPH-mediated nitrogen deletion, run in one pot with no evaporation or workup between steps, turns primary amines and aldehydes into new C-C bonds by cutting out the nitrogen that joined them. The hypothesis and baseline protocol came largely from Gemini and an AI collaborator called Maria, with chemists validating and then co-designing a high-throughput campaign that ran well over a thousand reactions.

original_title: Photocatalytic Halogen Atom Transfer from Phosphinic Chlorides Generates P-Centered Radicals and Enables Direct Hydrophosphonylation of Alkenes
title: Phosphorus radicals straight off the P-Cl bond for once
blurb: Industrial organophosphorus chemistry runs on phosphorus chlorides, but nobody had a photocatalytic way to turn P-Cl into a P-centered radical directly. This does it by halogen atom transfer, using cheap tertiary amines as the abstractor under blue LEDs, and routes the radicals straight into alkenes to make tertiary phosphine oxides in one step.

original_title: Nucleopalladation‐Enabled Synthesis of Nonproteinogenic α ‐Amino Acid Derivatives
title: Trapping the palladium intermediate long enough to build weird amino acids
blurb: Aminopalladation of alkenes usually stalls once the nitrogen goes on. Here the resulting organopalladium species gets pushed into a three-component carboamination of acrylamides instead, installing an amine and a carbon fragment across the same double bond in one step. That opens a path to nonproteinogenic amino acid derivatives outside the usual Michael-acceptor playbook, with a removable directing group to boot.

original_title: Pd-Catalyzed Divergent Annulation of 2-Aryl-1,3-dicarbonyls with Allenoates: Access to Benzo[ d ]oxepines and Spiroindanes
title: Same two reactants, three different ring systems depending on the metal
blurb: 2-aryl-1,3-dicarbonyls plus allenoates branch hard depending on catalyst: Pd gives either benzo[d]oxepines or spiroindanes depending on the substrate (a (5+2) versus (3+2) annulation), while swapping in Rh gets you spiroindenes instead. One enol-directed setup, divergent outcomes just by picking the metal.

original_title: Practical Ag-Catalyzed Multicomponent Reaction to Access 9-Phosphorylated Xanthenes
title: A five-step cascade under one silver catalyst to build phosphorylated xanthenes
blurb: 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde, secondary phosphine oxides, and beta-alkynyl ketones get stitched together under Ag catalysis through phospha-aldol, alkylation, cyclization, dehydration, and a second cyclization, all in one pot, to give 9-phosphorylated xanthenes. The mechanism isn't guesswork either, they tracked intermediates by in situ NMR and HRMS.

original_title: Multicomponent Synthesis of Aspartyl Hydrazide- and Hydroxamate-Containing Peptidomimetics
title: A carbodiimide multicomponent route to peptide mimics with built-in stability upgrades
blurb: A mild carbodiimide-based multicomponent reaction assembles hydrazide- and hydroxamate-containing peptidomimetics directly, scaffolds medicinal chemists like for their stability over plain peptide bonds. It tolerates a decent range of functional groups and peptide building blocks, and extends to N-amino peptidomimetics as well, leaving versatile handles for further derivatization.

original_title: Direct Photocatalytic Synthesis of 1,3,4-Oxa(thia)diazoles from Aldehydes and (Thio)hydrazides
title: An oxadiazole synthesis that doesn't care whether you keep the air out
blurb: An acridine photocatalyst converts (thio)semicarbazides and aldehydes into 1,3,4-oxa(thia)diazoles in a two-step, one-pot protocol, and it runs just as well with or without oxygen because the DCE solvent itself steps in as the oxidant when needed. Stern-Volmer quenching, radical traps, quantum yields, and cyclic voltammetry all point to oxidation of the in situ hydrazone through radical intermediates.

original_title: Access to Fluorinated Azetidines via Cobalt-Catalyzed Hydrosilylation of β-Lactams
title: Turning β-lactams into fluorinated azetidines, stereochemistry intact
blurb: A cobalt pincer catalyst hydrosilylates β-lactams with phenylsilane under mild conditions, delivering a broad set of 4-CF3 and 4-CHF2 azetidines in good yield with full retention of stereochemistry. The same protocol also runs on non-fluorinated lactams and acyclic amides to give pyrrolidines and tertiary amines, and there's an odd reductive decarboxylation on an ester substrate worth a footnote.

original_title: Rh2C3− Cluster-Driven Nitrogen Activation: Trapping a High-Energy Intermediate
title: Catching N2 mid-bond on a gas-phase rhodium carbide cluster
blurb: Gas-phase Rh2C3- reacted with N2 and probed by mass spec, photoelectron spectroscopy, and calculations shows the N2 attaches end-on without disturbing the cluster's electronic core, and that adduct is itself a trapped high-energy intermediate rather than the end point. Fundamental gas-phase work, nowhere near a working catalyst, but it's the kind of intermediate nitrogen-fixation mechanisms need pinned down.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Redox‐Active Oxamide–Nickel Complexes: Electronic Structures, Magnetic Properties, and Reactivity in C–C Bond Formation
title: Nickel complexes that let the ligand share the redox burden
blurb: A redox-active oxamide-aminophenol ligand gives a square-planar Ni(II) monomer alongside a trinuclear complex with tight Ni···Ni contacts, and the electrochemistry and magnetism confirm the ligand itself is picking up radical character, not just the metal. That cooperativity then gets put to work in C–C bond formation.

original_title: Molecular Origins of Chemoselectivity in Nickel‐Catalyzed N ‐Arylation: Ni–Amido Versus Ni–Nitrenoid Pathways
title: Why nickel N-arylation picks one mechanism over another
blurb: DFT on nickel-catalyzed N-arylation of sulfonamides, sulfinamides, amines, and indoles finds that for primary sulfonamides, direct reductive elimination off the Ni-amido intermediate just isn't kinetically feasible, so the real pathway runs through a further deprotonation step instead. No new reaction here, just mechanistic bookkeeping, but it's the kind of detail that decides which substrates actually work.

original_title: Hierarchically Porous Metal–Organic Frameworks as Multifunctional Platforms for Synergistic Chemo-Photo-Biocatalytic Enantioselective Synthesis
title: One MOF, three kinds of catalysis, one asymmetric product
blurb: A hierarchically porous UiO-67 MOF hosts a chemical catalyst and a photoenzyme together, running C2-alkylation straight into an asymmetric Mannich reaction in a single system. Stacking chemo-, photo-, and biocatalysis in one scaffold is still mostly aspirational as a field, so this reads more as a proof it can be done than a finished platform.

original_title: Synergistic Ethylene Glycol Synthesis via Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction Coupled With CH 3 OH Oxidation
title: CO2 and methanol combine to make ethylene glycol in one pot
blurb: Most paired photoredox setups just run CO2 reduction and a sacrificial oxidation side by side, using the electrons and holes separately with no real connection between them. This one couples them on purpose: a tandem photoredox-photothermal system reduces CO2 while oxidizing methanol with C–C coupling, so ethylene glycol comes out as the actual joint product rather than two unrelated half-reactions.

original_title: Visible-Light-Mediated Lewis Acid-Catalyzed 1,2-Cyclization of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes to Access 2-Azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptanes
title: Strained bicyclobutanes snap into fused azabicycloheptanes under visible light
blurb: A visible-light, Lewis acid-catalyzed radical cyclization fuses bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with N-allyl-N-chlorosulfonamides, forging three bonds and a fused azabicyclic ring in one step with solid chemo-, regio-, and diastereoselectivity. They also show the resulting bicyclic amines derivatize cleanly, so it's not just a one-trick cyclization.

original_title: Wavelength-controlled photothermal reduction of carbon dioxide to produce fuels over Nb 2 AlC/TiO 2 heterostructures in a continuous-flow reactor
title: A MAX phase teams up with TiO2 to push CO2 reduction with heat and light
blurb: A conductive Nb2AlC MAX phase coupled to TiO2 forms a heterostructure tested in continuous flow for photothermal CO2 reduction to fuels under solar radiation, with output apparently steerable by wavelength. Snippet's thin on the actual numbers, so that's the shape of the claim without the yields to back it yet.

original_title: Yttrium-90 resin microsphere radioembolization for post-liver transplantation recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma: a dual-center retrospective study
title: Y-90 radioembolization for HCC that came back after a transplant
blurb: A dual-center retrospective study on using Y-90 resin microsphere radioembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma that recurred after liver transplant. Retrospective and two centers, so it's real-world experience rather than a trial, but recurrent post-transplant HCC is exactly the population short on data.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Isolation of Open‐Shell Vinylidene Complexes of Iridium, Ruthenium, and Osmium
title: Isolating vinylidene radicals that usually blow themselves up
blurb: Open-shell vinylidene complexes normally burn through fast ligand-centered radical chemistry, but these paramagnetic Ir, Ru, and Os complexes with N-heterocyclic vinylidene ligands survive long enough under inert atmosphere to isolate on a prep scale, with crystal structures for Ir and Ru. EPR and computations put the radical on the vinylidene ligand itself rather than the metal.

original_title: Effects of Transglutaminase-Modified Indica Rice Flour on Structural, Textural Properties and Quality of Rice Noodles During Retrogradation.
title: Enzyme-crosslinked rice flour keeps noodles from going stale
blurb: Transglutaminase crosslinks the indica rice flour before the noodles are made, and the paper tracks what that does to structure and texture as the noodles retrograde and firm up on standing. Shelf-life food chemistry, standard texture metrics, nothing flashier than that.

original_title: Dioxygen Reactivity of Ni(II) Complexes with Redox-Active o -Aminophenolate Ligands
title: Nickel joins the o-aminophenolate dioxygen club
blurb: After building Fe and Co model complexes for the active sites of aminophenol dioxygenase and phenoxazinone synthase, they add Ni(II) analogues with the same redox-active o-aminophenolate ligands and look at how those react with O2. Whether nickel does anything the iron and cobalt versions didn't is the part worth waiting on.

original_title: Polymerization Induces Catalyst Microenvironment Variations
title: Watching a Grubbs catalyst get boxed in by its own polymer
blurb: An operando fluorescence lifetime method with a viscosity-sensing BODIPY rotor watches resin-supported Hoveyda-Grubbs catalysts during ROMP, and lifetimes climb as growing polymer progressively confines the catalyst, unevenly, down to the subparticle level. So nominally identical immobilized sites aren't actually seeing the same local environment once the polymer builds up around them.

original_title: Exploratory analysis of the association between nausea, vomiting, and fatigue in patients with metastatic breast cancer treated with trastuzumab deruxtecan
title: T-DXd's nausea and fatigue might be more tangled together than the antiemetic playbook assumes
blurb: NK1-antagonist regimens handle T-DXd's nausea and vomiting decently, but fatigue stays stubborn. This retrospective dig specifically asks whether nausea/vomiting and fatigue cluster together in metastatic breast cancer patients, rather than being separate side effects managed separately. Exploratory and retrospective, so a correlation flagged, not a mechanism explained.

original_title: Identifying SABRE-Active Iridium Complexes with Carboxylate Ligands through Relativistic DFT-NMR
title: Relativistic DFT finally tames iridium's NMR shifts
blurb: Predicting NMR shifts for SABRE-active iridium dihydrides needs spin-orbit corrections because iridium is heavy enough to break ordinary DFT. A 34-complex benchmark locks down a ZORA spin-orbit protocol for hydride shifts, then uses it to sort out coordination ambiguities in SABRE-active carboxylate complexes that were otherwise hard to assign.

original_title: Telix (ASX:TLX): Can the ASX 200 Radiopharma Group Secure Isotope Supply as the ITM Deal Nears? - Kalkine Media
title: Telix's isotope supply problem has a deadline now: the ITM deal
blurb: A market-watcher piece on whether Telix can lock down isotope supply before its ITM deal closes. Investor framing, not a result, so read it as a stock-page question mark rather than anything scientific.

original_title: Merging Pt-Doped TiO2 Photocatalysis with Nickel Catalysis Enables Redox-Reagent-Free Decarboxylative C(sp3)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling
title: A photocatalyst and a nickel catalyst split the redox work so no reagent has to
blurb: Pt-doped TiO2 photocatalysis paired with a nickel catalyst runs decarboxylative C(sp3)-C(sp2) coupling of carboxylic acids with aryl halides, no separate oxidant or reductant, even though the TiO2 conduction band and nickel's redox couples don't naturally match up. Works across a range of (hetero)aryl halides and the photocatalyst keeps performing over repeated reuse. Fewer stoichiometric redox reagents, if the workaround for that mismatch generalizes.

original_title: Desymmetrization of Acyclic meso ‐1,3‐Diols by Cu─H‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Silylation
title: Telling apart two mirror-image ends of a diol with a copper hydride
blurb: A Cu-H/(R,R)-Ph-BPE catalyst monosilylates meso-1,3-diols, picking one of the two chemically identical OH groups with high ee via Si-O coupling to a hydrosilane, no enzyme required. Getting the silane right, a tertiary homobenzylic one, was what stopped it from just silylating both sides, and a plain unsubstituted methylene at C2 gave the best results of the diols tried.

original_title: Synthesis of Functionalized 2 H -1,2,3-Triazoles by Electrooxidative Cyclization of α- tert -Butyliminyl Hydrazones
title: Electrochemistry builds triazoles straight from hydrazones
blurb: An electrooxidative cyclization turns alpha-tert-butyliminyl hydrazones into functionalized 2H-1,2,3-triazoles under mild conditions and scales to decagram quantities. They note it's the first electrochemical oxidation run on this class of hydrazone, so a genuinely new route rather than a greener rehash of an old one.

original_title: Indeno[1,2- b ]xanthene: A Formal Oxygen-Inserted Indeno[1,2- b ]fluorene as a Fully Conjugated Indenoxanthene Isomer
title: A pentacene-sized isomer built by swapping in an oxygen
blurb: Indeno[1,2-b]xanthene is a modular, oxygen-inserted version of indeno[1,2-b]fluorene, a 22pi-isoelectronic stand-in for pentacene built to chase anthrazulene, a reactive 14pi core nobody has actually isolated. Doping in that oxygen and varying substituents pushes more zwitterionic character into the ground state, giving bigger dipoles (about 9.6 D), both oxidized and reduced forms being accessible, and band gaps down around 1.2 eV. A stable proxy for a molecule that still doesn't exist on its own.

original_title: Diverse Pathways for Migration in Carbonylation: From Transition-Metal Catalysis to Radical Strategies
title: A review of carbonylation's migration problem
blurb: Migratory carbonylations shift the reactive site and drag a functional group along with it, and pinning down exactly where that group ends up is still the hard part. This review rounds up the tactics for controlling it, from transition-metal catalysis to radical approaches, with an eye on energy and chemical-engineering applications. It's a survey piece, so don't expect one new reaction to point to, just a map of the field.

original_title: PFLISA: A New Ultrasensitive, Multiplex Immunoassay Platform Enables Cytokine Network Profiling in Sepsis
title: A 96-well plate that can smell femtograms of cytokine
blurb: PFLISA pairs plasmonic-enhanced fluorescence with spatially encoded antibody spots to read out 12 inflammatory cytokines at once from just 15 µL of plasma, with limits of quantification as low as 3.4 fg/mL for the scarcest ones. That's the sensitivity you need to actually map a cytokine network in sepsis instead of just naming whichever one happens to be loudest. Still an assay validation, not a sepsis finding, but a genuinely useful instrument if the multiplexing holds up elsewhere.

original_title: Relative tracer delivery from [18F]MK6240 PET imaging as a perfusion-sensitive biomarker across aging and clinically defined cognitive impairment
title: MK6240 PET as a free perfusion readout
blurb: Using tracer delivery on MK6240 PET scans, a tracer normally run for tau, as a stand-in for brain perfusion across aging and cognitive impairment. Convenient if it checks out: one scan already being done, a second readout for free.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Beyond Lewis Acidity: Thiophilicity and Redox Stability as Design Principles for Sulphur‐Containing Polymerisation Catalysis
title: Lewis acidity doesn't explain these sulfur polymerization catalysts
blurb: ROCOP catalysts for sulfur-containing monomers are basically borrowed from all-oxygen chemistry, where activity tracks the rate-determining propagation step. Here that transfer fails: for Cr(III), Co(III), and Zn(II) salicylimine complexes, activity lines up better with off-cycle metal thiolates formed by side reactions than with anything in the main catalytic cycle. Thiophilicity and redox stability look like the real design levers, not Lewis acidity, which means a chunk of the standard catalyst playbook needs rewriting for these monomers.

original_title: Proteomics-Guided Aptamer Discovery for Molecular Recognition of Tenascin C in Tongue Squamous Cell Carcinoma
title: Found a tongue cancer marker by proteomics, then raised an aptamer against it
blurb: Comparing 37 paired tumor and normal tissue samples from oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma, quantitative proteomics flagged Tenascin C as the tumor-associated protein, and SELEX against it produced an aptamer for molecular recognition. A workable recipe for getting a detection reagent when nobody's handed you a reliable target.

original_title: Design, Synthesis, and Preclinical Evaluation of [18F]FPON, a First-In-Class PET Tracer Targeting Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen for Glioblastoma Imaging.
title: A PET tracer that targets PCNA instead of the usual glioma markers
blurb: [18F]FPON goes after proliferating cell nuclear antigen, a first-in-class target for glioblastoma PET imaging, carried through synthesis and preclinical evaluation. Preclinical only, so no human scans yet, but PCNA is at least a sensible thing to chase in a tumor defined by proliferation.

original_title: Aerobic Visible-Light Photocatalytic Oxyphosphorodithiolation of Alkenes to Access β-Keto Phosphorodithioates
title: A light-driven route to β-keto phosphorodithioates, no oxidant needed
blurb: Eosin B under visible light runs a three-component coupling of alkenes, P4S10, and alcohols in air at room temperature, going through a radical pathway with an in-situ phosphorodithioate intermediate. Broad scope, gram-scale, and a few of the products show moderate HepG2 inhibition, so there's a bonus lead for the med-chem side tacked onto what's otherwise a methodology paper.

original_title: Synthesis of Unsymmetrical Disubstituted 2,2’‐Bipyridine Ligands and Their Pd(II)‐NNC Pincer Complexes
title: Building lopsided bipyridines to make Pd pincer catalysts
blurb: A Stille coupling off a new stannylpyridine intermediate, itself made via Suzuki coupling, gives unsymmetrical 6,6'-bisaryl bipyridines that then ortho-palladate cleanly into neutral PdCl(NNC) pincer complexes. Those complexes catalyze cycloisomerization of alkynoic acids, so the ligand-design detour earns its keep.

original_title: HER2 µMap proximity labeling reveals functional interactors and resistance mechanisms
title: Mapping HER2's neighbors turns up a fix for trastuzumab resistance
blurb: µMap proximity labeling of the HER2 interactome in breast cancer cells fingers protein tyrosine phosphatase F as a growth regulator, and shows that galectin inhibition destabilizes HER2 enough to overcome trastuzumab resistance. A proximity-labeling study that actually lands on a druggable angle instead of just handing back a longer interactor list.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Alkene-Relayed Alkylation/Annulation of Aryl Iodides via Multicomponent C–H Activation
title: Pd catalysis builds succinimide-fused rings straight from aryl iodides
blurb: A maleimide-relayed, palladium-catalyzed multicomponent C–H activation cascade turns simple aryl iodides into succinimide-fused dihydrophenanthrenes and acenaphthenes, in three- or four-component versions, with good regioselectivity and moderate-to-good yields. Broad substrate scope, and the resulting polycyclic cores turn up a lot in bioactive molecules, so this isn't just a methodology flex.

original_title: Remote C(sp3)–H Functionalization via Visible-Light-Mediated Generation of Amidyl Radicals from Readily Accessible Arylsulfonamides
title: Peptides get their aliphatic C–H bonds functionalized by light-made amidyl radicals
blurb: Visible light turns readily made arylsulfonamides into amidyl radicals, with a benzothiazolesulfonyl group picked out as the efficient trigger, that reach remote sp3 C–H bonds. Works on amino acid and peptide derivatives and scales into continuous flow, and the mechanism checks out as single-electron transfer off the photocatalyst.

original_title: Bifunctional Trianthracene Hexaimide: Neutral State for Organic Thin‐Film Transistors and Radical Anion for Photothermal Conversion
title: A transistor material that doubles as a heater once you reduce it
blurb: Trianthracene hexaimide packs in enough imide groups to drop its LUMO to -4.11 eV, which makes it a solid n-type transistor in its neutral form and, once reduced to the radical anion, a photothermal converter instead. Two stable redox states doing two unrelated jobs out of one molecule is the actual trick here.

original_title: Sequence‐Retentive Upcycling of Polyamide 66 Into Quasi‐Alternating Biodegradable Polyesteramides With Closed‐Loop Recyclability
title: Nylon 66 gets upcycled into a biodegradable version of itself without going back to monomers
blurb: Instead of fully depolymerizing waste PA66, adipic acid-assisted acidolysis chops it into carboxyl-terminated oligomers that keep the amide sequence intact, then ester-containing segments stitch them back together into quasi-alternating polyesteramides. Billed as biodegradable and closed-loop recyclable, which is the part that'll need to survive more than one cycle to mean anything.

original_title: Zeno Trap-enabled Quadrupole-Scanning Data-Independent Acquisition in nanoflow Quantitative Proteomics and Immunopeptidomics
title: Scanning the quadrupole instead of stepping it, for DIA proteomics
blurb: A scanning-quadrupole DIA mode on SCIEX's ZenoTOF 7600+, aimed at nanoflow immunopeptidomics, leaning on Zeno trapping for more ion utilization and MS/MS sensitivity. The payoff is better quantitative performance on tryptic peptides at nanoflow scale, an instrument-vendor methods paper through and through.

original_title: Complementing Compendial Compliance: A Turbidity-Based Control Strategy for Benzyl Alcohol Quality in Parenteral Drug Products
title: Tracking down what actually makes benzyl alcohol go turbid in injectables
blurb: Benzyl alcohol lots can pass every compendial spec and still throw particulates and turbidity in the finished drug product, so they ran it down to one water-insoluble impurity via RP-HPLC and GC-MS and built an instrument-based spec around it. A real fix for a failure mode the existing compendial tests apparently can't catch.

original_title: Direct photochemical activation of aliphatic carboxylic acids toward phosphinylation via polarity-reversed Arbuzov process
title: Swapping the phosphorus flips a photoreaction from Norrish II to Norrish I
blurb: Running a polarity-reversed Arbuzov on aliphatic carboxylic acids turns them into acylphosphine oxides, and 365 nm light cleaves those via Norrish type I into acyl and phosphinoyl radicals, giving decarboxylative phosphinylation in good yield with broad scope. The neat part is that just changing the phosphorus group redirects the whole photochemistry from type II to type I.

original_title: Prediction of PD-L1 status and characterization of tumor subtype in NSCLC with static and abbreviated dynamic LAFOV [(18)F]FDG PET.
title: Guessing PD-L1 status off a PET scan instead of a biopsy
blurb: Uses static and shortened dynamic long-axial-FOV FDG PET scans to predict PD-L1 status and characterize tumor subtype in NSCLC, a noninvasive stand-in for a biomarker that currently requires tissue.
venue: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: Programmed switching gives multiblock copolymers of uniform composition
title: Multiblock copolymers that come out uniform instead of a gradient
blurb: A programmed-switching approach for building multiblock copolymers with uniform composition rather than the usual chain-to-chain drift.

original_title: Serum CEA, CA 19 - 9, and FDG PET/CT SUVmax in relation to histological subtype and overall survival in stage IV lung cancer.
title: CEA, CA 19-9, and PET SUVmax lined up against lung cancer subtype and survival
blurb: Checks how serum CEA, CA 19-9, and FDG PET/CT SUVmax track with histological subtype and overall survival in stage IV lung cancer. The kind of correlational readout that's useful for prognosis but won't change how anyone gets treated tomorrow.

original_title: Recent advances in ROS-generating polymeric nanoplatforms for smart drug delivery and therapeutic technologies.
title: A review lap around ROS-generating nanoplatforms for drug delivery
blurb: Rounds up the recent crop of reactive-oxygen-species-generating polymeric nanoplatforms built for smart drug delivery and other therapeutic uses. A survey, not a new result.

original_title: One‐Pot Synthesis of 7‐(thiomethyl)dibenzo[b, d]azepinones via a 7‐ Exo ‐Heck/thio‐Michael Cascade
title: Heck then thio-Michael, one pot, ring built and closed
blurb: A 7-exo Heck/thio-Michael cascade strings together dibenzo[b,d]azepinones carrying a thiomethyl group in a single pot, 38-99% yield across a wide range of biaryl and thiol partners with solid diastereoselectivity. It scales and tolerates cleavable protecting groups, so it's built for actually making the thing, not just the scope table.

original_title: Photoinduced Decarboxylative Acylation of Aminals: Rapid Access to α-Amino Ketones
title: Light and one iridium catalyst turn aminals into alpha-amino ketones
blurb: Visible light plus a single Ir photocatalyst couples bench-stable aminals with alpha-ketoacids to give alpha-amino ketones, 49 examples up to 88% yield, CO2 the only byproduct. It runs through radical-polar crossover rather than the radical-radical coupling the imine versions rely on, and still handles the bulky ortho-substituted cases.

original_title: A focus on lucigenin as a potent photoredox catalyst
title: Lucigenin moonlighting as a photoredox catalyst
blurb: That high excited-state reduction potential lets this old dicationic dye drive oxidative azolation of arenes that normally need pre-activation, and apparently across a broad substrate scope. Same molecule, new job title.

original_title: Al(3+)-Crosslinked Transparent Ionic Conductive PAA-Lysine Hydrogels Toward Flexible High-Sensitivity Electrochemical Sensors.
title: Aluminum-crosslinked hydrogels for stretchy sensors
blurb: Al3+ crosslinks a PAA-lysine network into a transparent, ionically conductive gel pitched at flexible, high-sensitivity electrochemical sensors. That's the whole pitch here, nothing more to go on.

original_title: Hydrogen-Bond Network-Assisted Ethylene and Hydrogen Photosynthesis from Methane over Isolated Ir Active Sites under Ambient Conditions
title: Methane to ethylene without burning light the whole way through
blurb: Single Ir atoms sitting on oxygen-vacancy-rich TiO2 convert methane into ethylene and H2, and the trick is that the Ir distorts the lattice enough to trigger spontaneous hydrolysis in humid air, hydroxylating the surface so exposed Ir sites can activate the first methane molecule before any light even hits it. Getting selective ethylene out of methane at all is the hard part here, given how easily the C-C coupling step runs away.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Enantioselective synthesis of β-aryl-β-acyl esters as unsymmetrical 1,4-dicarbonyl compounds via oxidative aryl rearrangement using λ 3 -perchrolate iodane
title: An iodane reagent rearranges its way to chiral 1,4-dicarbonyls
blurb: A λ3-perchlorate iodane drives an oxidative aryl rearrangement chemoselective enough to leave other functional groups alone, delivering unsymmetrical beta-aryl-beta-acyl esters as enantioenriched 1,4-dicarbonyls. The follow-up derivatizations are what actually argue these are useful building blocks rather than a one-off curiosity.

original_title: Alkylsilyl Peroxide-Enabled Copper-Catalyzed Asymmetric Three-Component Alkylarylation of Vinylarenes with Alkanes and Arylboronic Acids
title: Copper catalysis pulls radicals straight off plain alkanes for asymmetric arylation
blurb: An alkylsilyl peroxide generates alkyl radicals by HAT directly from feedstock alkanes, and a copper catalyst stitches them onto vinylarenes with arylboronic acids to give chiral 1,1-diarylalkanes enantioselectively. Skipping prefunctionalized radical precursors is the point, since balancing HAT with asymmetric metal catalysis is usually where these methods fall apart.

original_title: FDH- and CODH-based enzymatic CO2 conversion: matching biocatalysts, electron delivery, and reaction systems across shifting bottlenecks
title: Enzymatic CO2 conversion's bottleneck isn't the catalyst anymore
blurb: A review making the case that formate dehydrogenase and CODH-based CO2 conversion has moved past characterizing isolated catalysts, toward matching them with the right electron delivery, mass transport, and reaction engineering, since that's where the performance limits actually sit now.

original_title: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis
title: Living polymerization, run by enzymes instead of synthetic chemistry
blurb: An enzymatic method builds high-molecular-weight polysaccharides with the kind of controlled chain growth you'd expect from synthetic living polymerization, rather than the usual biosynthetic route. Nature paper, so the control is presumably the point.

original_title: Organobase-Promoted Selective aza-Annulation of N-Sulfonyl Imines with β-Ketodinitriles: Application to Sulfamidate-Fused Pyrroles and Chromeno[4,3- b ]pyrroles
title: DABCO cyclizes tricky dinitrile nucleophiles into fused pyrroles, no metal needed
blurb: A cheap organobase under O2 pushes N-sulfonyl imines and beta-ketodinitriles through Mannich addition, aza-cyclization, tautomerization, and aromatization in one pot, building sulfamidate-fused pyrroles and chromeno[4,3-b]pyrroles that come out carrying CN, NH2, and C=O handles for further work. Doing it metal-free is the notable part, since this kind of annulation usually leans on a metal catalyst.

original_title: Multicomponent Atom-Pair Replacement to Construct Pyrazolo[3,4- b ]pyrrolo[3,4- e ]pyridine Derivatives
title: Cracking open isoxazolones to build fused heterocycles in one pot
blurb: I2/DMSO drives a decarboxylative ring-opening of 3-aryl isoxazolones that swaps out an atom pair and stitches five components into a pyrazolo-pyrrolopyridine scaffold in a single tandem step. Mechanism's backed by control experiments and HRMS, and they're already eyeing it for tweaking drug-related scaffolds.

original_title: Geometry-Dependent 1LLCT–3LLCT Spin–Orbit Coupling in Pd(II) Pincer–Carbazolide Emitters
title: Why one Pd-pincer emitter phosphoresces and its cousins don't
blurb: Same family of Pd(II) pincer-carbazolide emitters, but PhPdCN phosphoresces while PyPdCN and PmPdCN give blue delayed fluorescence instead. TD-DFT mapping of the shared triplet and singlet states finds the donor-local triplet sitting at an identical 2.51 eV depth in all three, barely coupling to the charge-transfer singlet (2 cm-1-ish), so whatever splits their fates has to come from the other triplet state instead.

original_title: Synergistic Ethylene Glycol Synthesis via Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction Coupled With CH 3 OH Oxidation
title: Wiring CO2 reduction straight into methanol oxidation to make ethylene glycol
blurb: Most paired photoredox CO2 setups just run oxidation and reduction side by side, cashing in electrons and holes separately without the two reactions actually talking to each other. This one couples CO2 reduction to C-C coupling of methanol directly in a combined photoredox-photothermal system, so both halves feed into the same ethylene glycol product instead of running as two unrelated reactions sharing a cell.

original_title: Glutaraldehyde in Enzyme Immobilization Protocols.
title: The glutaraldehyde protocol everyone cites and nobody rereads
blurb: A methods chapter on using glutaraldehyde to immobilize enzymes. Just the protocol, no results to argue with.

original_title: TECR palmitoylation triggers a necrotic cell death program driving acute liver injury
title: A palmitoylation switch that pushes liver cells into necrosis
blurb: TECR palmitoylation kicks off a necrotic death pathway they're calling TPNCD, and blocking it, genetically or with a drug, protects against both immune- and drug-induced liver injury. Drug-induced liver injury is exactly the thing that kills otherwise-promising compounds in trials, so a druggable node here is worth watching.

original_title: Bioresponsive Lysosome-Targeting Chimeras for Targeted Protein Degradation.
title: LYTACs built to wait for a trigger before degrading their target
blurb: A bioresponsive take on lysosome-targeting chimeras, engineered to engage only once triggered rather than degrading their target protein constitutively.

original_title: Mechanochemical Synthesis of Ultra-High-Molecular-Weight Polydisulfides with Ball Milling
title: Ball milling lipoic acid into polymers, no solvent required
blurb: Ring-opening polymerization of lipoic acid and its derivatives run dry in a ball mill with a non-toxic organocatalyst, skipping the solvent-heavy, high-temperature route polymer chemistry usually needs and still landing ultra-high-molecular-weight polydisulfides. Mechanochemistry's old news for small molecules; doing it to polymers is the actual point here.

original_title: Enzyme-catalyzed synthesis of anticancer agents: a green chemistry approach toward sustainable drug development
title: A decade-plus roundup of enzymes making anticancer drugs
blurb: A review tallying biocatalytic routes to anticancer compounds across oxidoreductases, transferases, hydrolases, lyases, and engineered multienzyme systems, pulling from literature between 2015 and this year. It's a survey rather than new chemistry, so treat it as a map of where biocatalysis has actually paid off in oncology synthesis, not a single standout result.

original_title: Lewis Acid-Directed Oxygen-Down Interfacial Water Regulation Stabilizes Local pH for Robust High-Current-Density Propylene Epoxidation
title: Fixing the pH crash that kills electrochemical propylene oxide production
blurb: Bromine-radical propylene epoxidation looks good on paper until the anode acidifies itself at the current densities industry would actually need. A Cr-doped spinel cobalt oxide catalyst (Cr0.5Co2.5O4/CP) uses Lewis acid sites to orient interfacial water oxygen-down and hold the local pH steady, which is what lets the reaction keep running at high current instead of just surviving lab-scale conditions.
